summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a complex medical history including Crohn’s disease, chronic kidney disease, diastolic heart failure, and spinal degeneration was admitted for worsening lower back pain with new left leg weakness and urinary symptoms including dysuria and incontinence. Imaging revealed progressive disc bulges at L3-4 and L4-5 without acute surgical findings, and neurosurgery recommended continued medical management. A urinary tract infection was suspected despite a negative culture, leading to a short course of increased-dose ciprofloxacin. Her pain was managed with gabapentin and opioids, and she showed improvement in infection markers and kidney function. She was discharged home with instructions to complete the antibiotic course, follow up with primary care and pain management, and continue adjusted medications.
